text: Brief fact-check at 63 refine: the frozen-set deferral is pinned by TWO assertions, not the two the brief named. test/frozen-set-compiled.test.mjs:113-114 (deepEqual on compiled.deferred plus the installed exclusion) is a real pin that was NOT named; test/framework-stops-shipping-guard.test.mjs:52 IS named but is NOT a pin — its REMAINING table asserts each member's [id, enforcementPoint] pair, which stays true after gate-order compiles. A story briefed this way would have edited a control that was already true and missed one that was not. Lesson: when a brief hands you a pin set, re-derive it by grepping the assertion, not the mention.

aof graph impact can report a COMMENT-derived dependency as a real edge. src/work-loop.mjs is contractually import-free (53's work-loop-determinism), and the graph reports one outbound edge to src/loop-progress.mjs — extracted from the module's own header comment, which quotes the import that 69/06 added and F-69-V11 removed. Confirmed at source: the file has zero import statements. Lesson for every architect grounding a zero-import claim in the graph: graph impact is exact about edges it extracted, not about whether the extraction saw code or prose. Confirm a purity contract at source.

A frozen-set member deferred for a whole milestone can be UN-IMPLEMENTABLE as declared, and nothing notices. gate-order's rule is { argument: '--aof-gate-order' } at 'the worker launch envelope' — a flag claude does not have, so compiling it literally would break every worker launch. 55 shipped it as 'a spelling so downstream work has one'; the spelling turned out to have no referent, which the deferral hid for four milestones. Lesson: a declared-but-uncompiled member should owe a feasibility note naming the mechanism its rule would use, or the gap record is measuring the wrong thing — the gap was never 'compile the rule', it was 'decide what the rule means'.

Two smaller brief corrections found at 63 refine, both harmless here but worth the retro: (1) .aof/acceptor-criterion.jsonc has NO src/bundle/ shipped copy — only frozen-set.jsonc and loops/*.md are bundle assets (src/bundle/bundle.json), so the '.aof declaration precedent' is two instances, not three. (2) src/commands/ is at 92 flat siblings, not 91, and the growth is already ledgered as TECH_DEBT item 78 — the entry 62 was owed and wrote. Re-measuring a brief's counts costs one command and caught both.

ARCHITECT ERROR caught at Three Amigos, and the most dangerous kind: ADR-005 §4 instructed 'two pins widen by exactly their deferral lines'. Measured at source, that instruction would have BLINDED a control. test/arch/acd-frozen-set-compiled.test.mjs holds a LOCAL three-entry COMPILED_POINTS map and traceProblems continues past any member outside it, so editing only the deepEqual at :129 arms the fourth enforcement point and removes it from the trace in one commit — green while tracing nothing, which that file's own header says it was re-aimed to refuse. Lesson: when an ADR tells a builder to widen a delivered control, the architect must read the control's BODY, not its assertion line. 'Widen by exactly N lines' is a claim about a file you have not opened.

A shipped byte-identity claim has been false on every Windows checkout and no gate could see it. .gitattributes pins .aof/**/*.json, which does not match .jsonc, so .aof/frozen-set.jsonc is w/crlf while src/bundle/frozen-set.jsonc is w/lf eol=lf; their on-disk sha256 differ and the LF hash is the one src/bundle/manifest.json records. Git holds ONE blob for both, so the mismatch is invisible in a diff and passes Linux CI — it can only be seen with git ls-files --eol or an on-disk hash. Third instance of the species (TECH_DEBT item 8, the .aof/loops pin, this), so 63 takes a ratchet driven from the bundle's own asset list rather than a third path-specific line. Lesson: a byte-identity fitness function must assert the ATTRIBUTE, not only the bytes, or it is a control that can only fail on the maintainer's laptop.

REVIEWER RE-MADE THE MISTAKE THE MILESTONE HAD ALREADY RECORDED, one story later. At 63/02's structural review the architect cleared FF-6305's `pending` marker on the grounds that the control file had landed — but it had landed on the STORY BRANCH (aof/mesh/63-02), not on the milestone branch, and `aof work doctor 63` immediately turned that row's control-unresolved from a WARN into an unmarked ERROR. 63/01's own review had already written this rule into STATE.md verbatim for FF-6304 ("must flip from pending to its path AT MERGE and not before — flipping while the file is branch-only converts that warn into an unmarked failure"). Two causes, both mechanisable: (a) the architect's standing instruction says 'what clears pending is landing the file', and 'landed' is ambiguous between 'the developer wrote it' and 'it is on the branch the register is read from' — the instruction needs the second reading spelled; (b) nothing in the review loop runs `aof work doctor <ref>` after a register edit, so the check that catches it in one second is manual. FIX SHIPPED IN THE ARTIFACT: every remaining pending row in 63's register now carries the flip condition in its own cell ('built and green on <branch>; flips AT MERGE'), so the next reader cannot mistake reviewed for merged. Raised by: architect (63/02 review, self-reported)

A FITNESS LEG WHOSE ONLY KEEPABLE FORM IS NARROWER THAN ITS DECLARED CLAIM MUST NAME ITS RESIDUE IN THE REGISTER, or the row becomes a false receipt. FF-6305's row claimed 'no program spelling appears anywhere in src/ outside [the declaration]' (ADR-010 §2). Measured at 63/02's build: a literal ban on the program token reds eleven files — src/graph-faces.mjs:47 exports GRAPHIFY_SERVE_COMMAND = 'aof' as a genuine program, src/commands/loop.mjs:1746 holds route: ['work','loop'] — so the developer correctly narrowed the sweep to the ADJACENT literal run. But the adjacency form cannot see { program: 'aof', args: ['work','loop'] } or a template literal, which are the two shapes the defect would actually take, and which are exactly what ADR-010 §2 struck from ADR-006 §2. The narrowing was right; the register was wrong to keep claiming the broad property. Two lessons: (1) when I write a fitness row, I must write the form the check can actually take, having measured what a broad form would red — a row that states a property no keepable check can assert produces a green control and a false claim; (2) when a leg narrows at build time, the residue must be routed to a named sibling row in the same edit rather than left implicit. FIXED IN THE REGISTER: FF-6305's row now states the narrowing, the measurement that forced it and the residue; FF-6306 gains the residue leg in the form the defect takes (no program/bin/command key assigned a string literal in the three mesh files; no template literal interpolating a scope after a command prefix), which is where a second speller would actually be authored. Raised by: architect (63/02 review)

GRAPH-DERIVED COUPLING CAN BE MANUFACTURED BY COMMENTS, and a reach pin is not the graph. At 63/03's structural review 'aof graph impact src/work-loop.mjs' reported one outbound edge, src/loop-progress.mjs. work-loop.mjs imports NOTHING: the only occurrences of that path are in a comment at :7 and a prose note at :265, and 53/ADR work-loop-determinism exists precisely because a real import there once made the module unloadable in isolation. Graphify's extraction counted the prose. Consequence if trusted: 63/03's mesh-blind reach pin moves 67 to 68 on the claim that work-loop.mjs is a zero-import leaf, and a reviewer checking that claim against the graph alone would have read a second node and called the pin wrong. Checked at source instead, and the pin is right. Lesson: the graph is advisory and its edges are a SUPERSET of the import closure; any leg that turns on 'imports nothing' must be read from the module, never from graph impact.

A STORY CONTRACT CAN PIN THE SHAPE OF ITS OWN FIX SHUT. 63/03's task 04 pins six spawn-seam forwards as bare shorthand keys, and FF-6306's fence leg asserts it — which is exactly the edit the premature-done hazard needs (hand a loop launch a loop-shaped transcript watch instead of the session-shaped default). So the story that EXPOSED the defect is the one story structurally forbidden from fixing it, and the fix needed an architect ruling (ADR-013) plus a follow-up story before a line could be written. This is not a mistake by anyone: the fence was right to exist and the builder was right to flag rather than breach it. But a fence written as 'these six forwards are bare' asserts a MECHANISM where the invariant is a PROPERTY ('no launch DECISION reaches the fenced machinery') — and a mechanism-shaped invariant forbids correct implementations along with incorrect ones. Lesson: when writing an out-of-scope fence, assert the property the fence protects, not the current spelling of the code that satisfies it; otherwise the fence bills the next legitimate change an ADR.

Red-probing a fitness function in ONE node process reports a live control as vacuous. Mutating a source file and then re-importing the arch test with a cache-busting query string does NOT reload the module under test: the arch test's own static import of that module resolves to the same URL and is served from the module cache, so every RUNTIME leg silently re-runs against the unmutated code and reports green. At 63/04's review this made six of FF-6307's eight legs look like controls that held nothing; re-running each probe in a FRESH process turned all six red. A second trap in the same session: a String.replace anchor of '  return decided.admitted === true' landed on an EARLIER matching line in containingDriver rather than throughTheLoop, so the intended mutation never reached the code path and again read as a vacuous control. Rule for red probes: one fresh process per mutation, and assert the mutated site (not just that the patch applied).
